title: Red Cabbage and Apple Coleslaw
subtitle: Crunchy red cabbage and sharp apple slaw with a light vinaigrette
excerpt: Finely shredded red cabbage with coarsely grated sharp apple and carrot, dressed with cider vinegar, Dijon and a little honey. Vivid in colour, crunchy, and very good with roast pork or cold cuts.
sourceNotes: Red cabbage slaws with apple are common in British and American autumn cooking, building on the traditional pairing of red cabbage and apple in braised form. The vinaigrette version (rather than mayo) is well documented in British salad cookbooks from the 1980s onward.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Colour will deepen and intensify as it sits.

content.text: Red cabbage and apple coleslaw is a vegan slaw with a vivid purple colour and a crunch that holds for two days in the fridge. The sharp apple brings acidity; the cider vinegar dressing adds more. A little honey rounds the whole thing out. It is particularly good with roast pork, cold ham, or any rich meat that benefits from a sharp, fresh counterpoint.

items.prepNote: outer leaves removed, finely shredded, about 600 g prepared
cored and coarsely grated, skin left on

content.text: Combine the shredded red cabbage, grated apple and carrot in a large bowl. Whisk together {{cider-vinegar}} of cider vinegar, {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{honey}} of honey, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss until everything is coated. Taste and adjust for seasoning or sharpness. Serve immediately or refrigerate for up to 2 days.

items.fix: Toss the grated apple with the dressing immediately after grating, or add a squeeze of lemon to the apple before mixing. The vinegar in the dressing does the same job but takes a moment to coat.

items.cause: Eating apple was very tart, or excess vinegar.
items.fix: Add another teaspoon of honey and toss. A sweeter apple (Cox, Braeburn) will also make a milder slaw.

content.text: Red cabbage and apple is a good autumn pairing in British cooking: the same combination that works braised turns out to work raw too. The vivid purple slaw suits a Christmas buffet table, a late-autumn dinner plate next to a pork chop, or a lunchbox alongside cold sliced meat.
